**The judgement call worth recording: I did *not* move `Real.arctan_div_add_arctan_div` too.** It
sits in the same file with the same shape — implicit reals plus positivity hypotheses, no `Real`
receiver — so the finding's stated rule ("not dot notation on a `Complex` object") would appear to
condemn it equally, and the tempting move was to "fix both while I'm here". But Mathlib's own
`Real.arctan_inv_of_pos`, of which this is the direct quotient-form companion, has exactly that

The `Complex` case is different because the theorem is not about a complex operation at all — it is
about real arctangents cast into `ℂ`. The reviewer read both and flagged one; that asymmetry was
correct, and over-applying the rule would have been a fresh finding rather than a fix.

**documentation** — the module docstring of `Topology/Order/OrderClosed.lean` listed its theorem
without saying what it is for. Added the purpose: an estimate proved by a limiting argument arrives
as `v ≤ K + e i` with `e` vanishing, and this discharges the error term in one step so a proof need
not repeat the limit argument at each estimate.

Both files rebuild, all three linters clean, no long lines. PR body names neither declaration, so no
drift to repair.

## r742 — R5 attempted on ADS Layer 7.1, and stopped: Mathlib's density predicate is opaque

R1–R4 were empty (three PRs in flight, all scoreboards stale against their new heads, #6110's green
build only 18 minutes old), so this was an authoring round.

**Target chosen by working backwards from the question Chris asked at r739.** Dirichlet-density
Chebotarev is Chebotarev Layer 10; the first *buildable* thing on its critical path is not in the
Chebotarev roadmap at all but in mine: **ADS Layer 7.1**, whose finite-error / squeeze /
normalization / contraction lemmas Chebotarev Layer 3 consumes. Checked and confirmed absent: no
such lemma in TauCeti `main`, no `DirichletDensity` module, no open PR anywhere claiming it, and
`HasDirichletDensity` appears in TauCeti only inside two `ResidueDegree.lean` docstrings.

**Then the target turned out to be blocked upstream.** Mathlib's
`NumberTheory/NumberField/DirichletDensity.lean` defines `HasDirichletDensity` as a plain `def`
under `public section` with **no `@[expose]` and no characterisation lemma**. From a module-system
file — which every TauCeti file is — the definition cannot be unfolded even by a direct
definitional check, so **nothing in TauCeti can prove or consume a `HasDirichletDensity` fact at
all**. That is why `ResidueDegree.lean` only ever mentions it in prose; the pattern was visible in
the corpus before I understood it.

Three probes, because the first result was misleading:

1. a **classic** (non-`module`) file accepts `h : S.HasDirichletDensity δ` where a `Tendsto` is
   expected — this is what made me think the route was open;
2. the same probe **as a module file** fails with "definitions were not unfolded because their
   definition is not exposed";
3. `attribute [expose] NumberField.Set.HasDirichletDensity` in the importer is rejected outright —
   "can only be added when declaring a `def`". **An importer cannot unlock it.**

Note the trap in probe 1: a scratch probe written without `module` does not model this repo, and
answered the opposite of the truth. **Probe in the dialect of the file you are going to write.**

**Stopped rather than shipping a crippled module.** The bounds themselves are expressible — they
only mention `primeIdealZetaSum`, which does export `primeIdealZetaSum_def` — but their entire
purpose is the squeeze, whose conclusion *is* `HasDirichletDensity`. A module with the two
definitions and no bridge would advance nothing and would invite exactly the `scope` block that
#6051 earned at r699. Draft kept at
`scratchpad/ads-layer-7.1-dirichlet-density-bounds.lean.draft`; branch deleted, no PR opened.

**Reported to Chris**, who is one of the three authors of the Mathlib file, so the one-line upstream
fix is his to make.

## r743 — R5: Layer 3.4's branch, opened as #6145

R1–R4 empty: three PRs in flight, all three builds green but every scoreboard stale against its new
head, and the oldest green build (#6110, 15:36) still short of the R4 hour.

**Target found by re-costing after this morning's merges.** ADS 7.1 is blocked upstream (r742), but
**Layer 3.4's second half became reachable today**: #6051 (the expansion) merged at 09:14 and #6102
(nonvanishing) at 08:55, and `TauCeti.exists_differentiableOn_eqOn_exp_comp` — the holomorphic
branch on a simply connected domain — has been on `main` all along in `Analysis/Complex/`. Three
ingredients, all present, none of which I had put together before. **The lesson: a merge does not
only clear the PR that merged; re-cost the parked work every time one lands.**

Shipped: `exists_differentiableOn_exp_eq_LSeries` — on a simply connected open `U` where the
`L`-series is holomorphic and the ideal series converges absolutely pointwise, there is a
holomorphic `L` with `exp ∘ L` the `L`-series **and** `deriv L = logDeriv` of it. Plus the general
`deriv_eq_logDeriv_of_eqOn_exp_comp` in `BranchLogRoot.lean`, where the branch machinery lives.

**Zero-freeness is derived, not assumed.** The roadmap phrase is "on a simply connected zero-free
region", and it would have been easy to take zero-freeness as a hypothesis. It is not one here: it
comes from the Euler product via the convergence hypothesis, so a caller supplies a region of
absolute convergence rather than one it has already had to prove zero-free. That is strictly more
useful and it is what #6102 bought.

Two small things worth keeping:

* `logDeriv` appears in a **statement**, so its home had to be a `public import`. It was already
  imported plainly, and `SpecialFunctions.Complex.LogDeriv` *public*-imports `Calculus.LogDeriv`, so
  promoting the existing line was enough — no new import, still minimal and non-redundant.
* `#check`-ing the elaborated statements before believing the file (the r740 habit) is now routine;
  both printed as intended.

The Main-statements list in `BranchLogRoot.lean` was updated in the same commit, since a docstring
that omits a new public theorem is itself a finding.

## r744 — re-costed the parked PRs; #6058 went ten-of-ten; corrected a false supersession

#6058 is **ALL-GREEN at head** (16:22) — the `naming` and `documentation` fixes from r741 both took.
R4 was not due on #6110 (48 minutes since its green build, threshold 60), so instead of idling I
re-costed the four parked PRs, which is the r743 lesson applied deliberately rather than by luck.

**#5586: the parking reason was wrong, though the parking was right.** Its title said "superseded by
#5538" — but **#5538 was CLOSED, not merged**, so on its face the supersession never happened and
the PR was live work I had abandoned. Checked properly instead of assuming either way: all four
headline declarations *are* on `main`, and `git log` on the file that holds
`inf_eq_bot_of_unramified` names **#5633** — my own auxiliary-prime PR, which absorbed the material
when I unstacked it at r720. So the PR is genuinely dead, by a different route than recorded.

Title and body corrected with the evidence table, and the title now says "please close". **I did not
close it** — closing is CI's job, not this loop's.

The general point: **"superseded by #N" is a claim with an expiry date.** #N can be closed rather
than merged, and then the note is worse than no note, because it reads as settled. A supersession
claim should name the *declarations* and where they landed, which survives whatever happens to #N.

**#5572 stays parked, and I checked rather than assumed.** Its `scope` finding says: "Defer this PR
until Layer 3.4's derivative exists on main or in an open PR." It was tempting to unpark it on the
strength of #6145, opened last round — but #6145 gives the *branch* and identifies `deriv L` with
`logDeriv`, and Layer 3.4's derivative component is the **prime-power series** for that logarithmic
derivative, which nothing yet provides. The condition is not met. Unparking on a near-miss would
have been the wrong kind of eagerness; the r738 unparking of #6051 was right precisely because its
condition genuinely *was* met.

That said, the check paid for itself: it names the next authoring target exactly — the prime-power
expansion of `logDeriv (LSeries χ)`, which is the natural successor to #6145 and unparks #5572.

## r746 — R3 on #6110: four findings, and the reversal that was not worth contesting

The review I withheld R4 from at r745 landed at 16:40:56, **at head**. The `reuse` block is gone —
the r738/r739 fix took — and four `request_changes` replaced it: `api-design`, `naming`,
`proof-quality`, `documentation`. `3a2def355e` → `88bc15e24c`.

**The interesting part is that round 2 reverses round 1, and I did not contest it.** Verbatim:

* round 1 `reuse` (block, 09:29): "`comap_mapRingEquiv_eq_bot_iff` is an unnecessary public
  specialization of existing generic lemmas. *Fix:* **Keep it private or delete it**; at consumers
  rewrite with `← Ideal.map_symm` and apply `Ideal.map_eq_bot_iff_of_injective ...` directly."
* round 2 `proof-quality` (16:40): "Both subtype constructors prove comapped ideals nonzero by
  unfolding `Ideal.map_symm` and injectivity internals … *Fix:* **Make
  `comap_mapRingEquiv_eq_bot_iff` public** and use it for both nonzero proofs."

Round 2 condemns precisely the code round 1's instruction produced. That is the contest criterion —
"a later round reverses an earlier one" — and I had both texts quotable. **I still did not contest,
because a third configuration satisfies everything**, which is the r718→r729 pattern:

round 1's objection was to a *public specialization living inside an arithmetic-functions file*.
`api-design` this round says the same three lemmas "mention no arithmetic-function types and are
general ideal/RingOfIntegers transport infrastructure", and asks for a canonical module; `naming`
asks for the `Ideal` namespace. Moving them there makes them general transport API rather than a
specialization hidden in the wrong file — a different object from the one `reuse` blocked. So
`api-design` + `naming` + `proof-quality` are jointly satisfiable, and contesting would have spent a
thread to defend code all three dislike.

**The check that made this decidable:** `naming` offered "or keep them private", which looked like
the cheap way out — but `_refl` and `_trans` are used from `NormCoeff.lean`, a different file, so
private was never available. Reading the *use sites* rather than the fix text settled which branch
of the offered fix was real.

New module `NumberTheory/NumberField/RingOfIntegers/Transport.lean`: two functoriality lemmas on
elements plus the three comap lemmas, `Ideal` namespace, ideal argument first for dot notation,
`@[simp]` as normal forms. Both consumer proofs in `normCoeff_map` now call the named lemma instead
of unfolding internals. Imports are plain, not `public`, in both `Basic` and `NormCoeff` — the
lemmas appear only in proofs there.

Verified: Basic, NormCoeff and all five downstream importers build; three linters clean; no long
lines; no stale `IdealArithmeticFunction.comap_*` references anywhere.

## r747 — R3 on #6126: the analytic work I had put in the hypotheses

**#6058 merged.** #6126 came back blocked again at head, but on a *different* correctness point —
round 1's "add both forms" was satisfied, and round 2 says the forms are hollow: "Both the off-norm
theorem (`herr`) and limiting theorem (`hdom`) assume the required error summability/uniform
domination instead of deriving it from `LSeriesSummable f c`; thus they do not establish Layer 6.4's
formulas for an absolutely convergent L-series."

That is correct, and worse, **I had written the deferral into the PR body as if it were a virtue** —
"taken as an argument rather than manufactured". Taking the central estimate as a hypothesis is not
a design choice, it is the theorem not being proved. `6b644226bd` → `c0c79e6137`.

Both hypotheses are now constructed:

* **Summability**: beyond `2 x` the ratio `x / n` is at most `1 / 2`, so `|log (x / n)| ≥ log 2` and
  the `n`-th error is a fixed multiple of `‖LSeries.term f c n‖`. `summable_norm_iff` turns
  `LSeriesSummable` into absolute convergence and `Summable.of_norm_bounded_eventually_nat` discards
  the finitely many indices below `2 x` in one step.
* **Domination**: for `T ≥ 1` the kernel at a ratio `y` is bounded by that same error plus `1` once
  `y > 1 / 2` — and only finitely many `n` put `x / n` above `1 / 2`, so the `1` is summable against
  `‖f n‖`. Below `1 / 2` the sharp step vanishes and the error alone suffices.

**The catch I nearly shipped.** My first working version needed `hoff : ∀ n, x ≠ n` on the limiting
theorem, because the Layer 6.3 estimate excludes the ratio `1`. That builds, and no rubric had asked
about it — but it would have made the limiting form inapplicable at integer `x`, which is **exactly
the case the half-weight theorem exists for**, silently undoing round 1's requirement. The fix is
cheap once seen: at `y = 1` the kernel is exactly `π⁻¹ arctan (T / c)`, so `‖·‖ ≤ 1` uniformly, and
the endpoint needs no exclusion at all. **A hypothesis added to make a proof go through is a claim
about the theorem; check what it excludes against what the theorem is for.**

Cleanup forced two extractions and one restructure: the domination bound is now stated for a *ratio*
`y` with no `n` in it, which is both the honest statement and what brought every proof under thirty
lines (longest now 30). Body corrected — the sentence advertising the hypotheses is gone.

## r749 — R3 on #6145: both findings were the same criticism I had just accepted on #6126

The review I twice withheld R4 from landed at 17:13:56 at head. Two `request_changes`, and both were
right. `a73984487d` → `8da4ef95af`.

**`generality`** — the branch theorem assumed `hdiff : DifferentiableOn ℂ (LSeries …) U`. It does not
need to: `U` is open, so each `s ∈ U` has a point of `U` slightly to its left, and `hconv` there puts
`s` strictly right of the abscissa of absolute convergence. Three steps, all already on `main` or in
Mathlib: `LSeriesSummable_normCoeff` (the ideal-to-regrouped bridge, in `Regroup.lean`),
`LSeriesSummable.abscissaOfAbsConv_le`, and `LSeries_hasDerivAt`.

**This is the same defect as #6126's second correctness block, two rounds apart, and I wrote both.**
There I assumed the error summability; here I assumed holomorphy. In each case the hypothesis was
true, easy to state, and made the proof go through immediately — and in each case it moved the work
out of the theorem and onto every caller. **The tell is a hypothesis that the other hypotheses
already imply**, which is exactly what [[extraction-copies-scope-into-signatures]] warns about for
extraction; I had not been applying it to hypotheses I *chose* while authoring.

**`reuse`** — `deriv_eq_logDeriv_of_eqOn_exp_comp` differentiated the exponential and cancelled it by
hand, which is `logDeriv_comp` plus `Complex.logDeriv_exp`. The proof is now eight lines instead of
twelve and rests on Mathlib. One wrinkle: `logDeriv_congr_nhds` returns an `EventuallyEq`, not a
pointwise equality, so it needs `.eq_of_nhds` before it can be rewritten with.

Both new imports are plain rather than `public`: `Trigonometric.Deriv`, `LSeries.Deriv` and
`Regroup` are used only inside proofs.

Verified: both files build, both linters clean, no long lines, and **both real downstream importers
of `BranchLogRoot.lean`** (`Conformal/DiscInjection` and `Conformal/Koebe`) still build — that file
is shared with the Riemann-mapping work, so it is not a file to change casually. The one proof in it

## r752 — the r751 "gap" was already on main; correcting it, and the fifth false absence

Board: no red builds, no findings at any current head, #6126 under live review, #6110 and #6145 both
short of the R4 hour. So R5 — and I started the port I had scoped at r751.

**It was already done.** Opening `Frobenius/Tower.lean` to decide where the new theorem should live,
I found **`restrictScalars_eq_of_inertiaDeg_eq_one`** on line 230: precisely the element-level
E-bridge I had called "the genuine gap, unclaimed by any open PR", with a docstring that reads *"This
is the case a fixed-field fibre count runs through"* — written for the very consumer I was about to
write it for. One step further and it would have been a duplicate PR.

**Why I missed it: I grepped the *source's* name against the destination.** `chebotarev-density`
calls it `arithFrobAt_restrictScalars_eq`; TauCeti calls it `restrictScalars_eq_of_inertiaDeg_eq_one`,
because a good port renames to fit the destination's conventions. Grepping the source's name across
`main` returns "absent" essentially by construction. Memory written
([[search-the-destination-vocabulary]]) — it is the fourth distinct way a search lies to me, after
"never ran", "returned noise" and "wrong corpus": right corpus, clean run, **wrong vocabulary**.

That is **five false absences in one session**, and the fix is not another grep flag. It is: to
decide whether a result exists, *open the file that would own it and read its declaration list*. A
name grep answers "is this identifier present", which is a much weaker question than "is this result
present".

**Where Layer 8 actually stands**, by reading rather than grepping. `Frobenius/` has the full
element-level tower API (`restrictScalars_eq_pow_inertiaDeg`, the degree-one specialisation,

complement. Layers 1, 2 and 8.1 are done.

## r753 — R3 on #6110; #6145 went ALL-GREEN and #6126's correctness block cleared

Three results at once. **#6145 is ALL-GREEN at head** (17:53) after r749's two fixes — the branch of
the logarithm is done and waiting on the merge step. **#6126's `correctness` block is gone**: r747's
derivation of the convergence hypotheses satisfied it, and the reviewer, now able to see past the
block, returned eight `request_changes` on the other rubrics. **#6110** came back with a single
`api-design` request. `88bc15e24c` → `79344ff276`.

Took #6110 because one finding can be finished inside a round and eight cannot.

**The finding corrected my own reasoning about imports, and it was right.** I had made
`Basic.lean`'s `Transport` import plain on the grounds that the transport lemmas appear there only
inside proofs. But `Basic`'s *own statements* — `map_apply` and `zeroExtend_map` — expose
`Ideal.comap` terms, so an importer of `Basic` meets those terms and needs the `@[simp]` lemmas that
normalise them. The rule "public iff it appears in statements" is about **what the module's
statements put in front of importers**, not merely which names its proofs mention; I had been
reading it too narrowly. Also tagged `normCoeff_map` `@[simp]`, matching its neighbours.

**One consequence the finding did not mention, and I handled before it becomes next round's
finding:** once `Basic` publicly re-exports `Transport`, `NormCoeff`'s own plain import of it is
redundant, and import hygiene has been ruled on three times in this lane. Removed; everything still
builds. **Making an import public can make a *different* import redundant** — check the transitive
consequence in the same commit, not the next round.

Verified: five ADS modules build, both linters pass — including `simpNF` on the newly tagged lemma,
which is the linter that would object to a bad simp normal form.

## r754 — R3 on #6126: all eight findings, in one pass

`c0c79e6137` → `7e19c81eac`. With the correctness block gone the reviewer went through everything,
and every one of the eight was fair; none was worth contesting.

* **placement** — `Perron.lean` and `PerronFormula.lean` become `Perron/Basic.lean` and
  `Perron/Formula.lean`. `git mv` kept both as renames in the diff, which matters: a rename shows the
  reviewer the real change instead of a delete-plus-add of 300 lines.
* **naming** — `_apply` misclassifies a lemma that merely restates a definition; both are now `_def`,
  eight occurrences, no stale references.
* **api-design** — three parts: the endpoint limit now has a direct statement
  (`tendsto_truncatedPerron_LSeries_natCast`), the `integral_tsum` side condition is `private`, and
  the two zero values are `@[simp]`.
* **generality** — `term_mul_perronIntegrand` used `hx` only as `hx.le`, so `0 ≤ x` suffices.
* **reuse** — the vertical-line bound was eight lines of manual `norm_div`/`cpow` unfolding; it is
  `LSeries.norm_term_le_of_re_le_re f (by simp) n`, one line.
* **proof-quality** — the three `show` steps are named facts now.
* **documentation** — every "Layer 6.3" replaced by mathematical wording. **Roadmap layer numbers
  are process-relative and do not belong in a library docstring**; they read as structure to a future
  reader who has no roadmap. Six occurrences, all mine.
* **attribution** — a References section citing Davenport chapter 17.

**The one that needed judgement was `proof-quality` on the interchange.** The objection was that the
proof leaned on `LSeries f s` unfolding definitionally to `∑' n, term f s n` inside a rewrite chain.
Mathlib exports **no** equation lemma for `LSeries` — it is a plain `def` and `LSeries_congr` is the
only nearby API — so `rfl` is the only route. The fix was therefore not to remove the dependency but
to **name it**: a `have hLSeries : ∀ t, … := fun _ ↦ rfl` with a comment saying why it exists, then
`simp only [hLSeries]`. The proof no longer depends on the reader noticing an unfolding.

The 72-line proof in `Basic.lean` is pre-existing merged code carried through the rename, not mine
to decompose in this PR.

## r755 — R1 on #6126: my own rename collided with #6058 landing

**#6058 merged** (`2f71ccdae7`, the Perron rectangle decomposition) — the PR I fixed at r741 is in.
It edits `Perron.lean`, and r754's placement fix *renames* that file, so #6126 flipped to
`CONFLICTING` within minutes. `7e19c81eac` → `c948df99e7`.

The rebase itself was clean — git matched the rename against the edit. **But "successfully rebased"
proves nothing, and here the specific danger was one I created myself:** r754's
`perronIntegrand_apply` → `perronIntegrand_def` rename ran over *my* copy of the file, before #6058's
version existed on my branch. Any new use of the old name arriving with #6058 would have been
carried in stale and unrenamed.

Checked rather than assumed: no `_apply` references survive anywhere, #6058's own additions
(`arctan_corner_sum_eq_two_mul_pi_mul_I`, `le_of_eventually_le_add`) are present in the renamed file,
both modules build, both linters pass.

**The general shape is worth naming: a rename in my branch and an edit on main are a conflict class
that git resolves silently and wrongly-in-spirit.** Git reconciles the *file*; it cannot know that my
branch also renamed *declarations inside it*, so incoming uses of the old names ride in untouched.
The check after any rebase that carries a rename is: grep for every old name, then build.

Also of note: **#6145 and #6058 are both `UNKNOWN`/merged** — the merge queue is moving again, and
#6145 (ten-of-ten green) is being taken.

## r756 — started Layer 8.2, hit an instance wall, stopped with a diagnosis

Board quiet: #6145 merging, #6126 rebuilding after r755's rebase, #6110 green and awaiting review
(its hour is 19:20). Nothing at R1–R4, so R5.

Confirmed first that `zpowers_eq_stabilizer_of_isArithFrobAt` — the K-level "Frobenius generates the
decomposition group" — is on `main`, by **reading `DecompositionGroup.lean`** rather than grepping.
So the first absent link in the fibre-count chain is its **E-relative** form: for
`E = L^⟨σ⟩` and `Frob_K(Q) ∈ ⟨σ⟩`, the decomposition group of `Q` inside `Gal(L/E)` is everything.

The mathematics is three lines — `Gal(L/E) = ⟨σ|_E⟩` by `zpowers_toFixedFieldAlgEquiv_eq_top`, and
`σ|_E` stabilises `Q` because `σ` does. **The obstacle is not mathematical but instance plumbing**:

```
failed to synthesize  MulAction Gal(L/↥(fixedField (Subgroup.zpowers σ))) (Ideal (𝓞 L))
```

Five probes, and the informative one is the contrast. Inside a tactic block, after
`set E := fixedField (Subgroup.zpowers σ)`, the statement **elaborates fine**. Written at
theorem-signature level with the fixed field spelled out inline, it fails — and adding
`IsScalarTower`, `NumberField ↥E`, `IsGalois ↥E L` and `IsGaloisGroup` to the statement, which is the
full set the source file carries, does not rescue it. So instance search behaves differently on the
unfolded term than on an opaque local: something is not firing through the
`IntermediateField.fixedField` coercion at the transparency the signature elaborator uses.

**That points at the design the first PR of this chain should establish**: give the fixed field a
*named definition* of its own — the field `E` attached to `σ` — and register the tower, number-field
and Galois instances against that name, so every later statement in the chain can say `Gal(L/E)`
without carrying four `haveI`s in its signature. The source repo sidesteps this by keeping everything
`private` inside one file and threading `haveI`s through each statement; a library API cannot.

**Stopped rather than forcing it.** Nothing committed, scratch branch deleted, probes are in the
scratchpad. This is now a design decision to make deliberately rather than a lemma to grind out at
the end of a round — and it is the honest reason this chain has not started, rather than the "next
round" I have written three times.

## r757 — #6145 merged; declined to unpark #5572 on a reading I do not believe

**#6145 is merged** — the holomorphic logarithm of an ideal `L`-series is on `main`, two rounds after

expansion (#6051). It would have been easy, and defensible-sounding, to mark the PR ready and let
the reviewer re-adjudicate.

**I did not, because I do not believe the condition is met.** Layer 3.4's third part is *the
derivative of the expansion* — a prime-power series for `logDeriv` — and #6145 gives the derivative
*of the branch*, identified as `logDeriv`, which is a different object. Pushing it back would be

**But silence is how a PR becomes abandoned**, which Chris warned about explicitly. So the state is
now written on the PR: a table of Layer 3.4's three parts, which two have landed and where, what
the remaining one is, and the single sentence that unparks it — *the prime-power series for
`logDeriv (LSeries χ)`*. Same treatment as #5586 and #6038 got: **a parked PR should carry its own
unparking condition, so the next reader does not have to re-derive it.**

That missing piece is also the natural successor to #6145 and the thing that makes Layer 3.4
complete, so it is the strongest authoring target in the ADS half of the lane — ahead of the

## r758 — R3 on #6110: the import rule is about the public surface, not the line count

`79344ff276` → `c2e3bf395b`. One real finding — `api-design` again; the other nine rubrics are
`stale`, not adverse, because the reviewer re-ran only the one that was blocking. Worth noting for
board reading: **`stale` and `blocking_request` both print as "not green", and only one of them is
work.**

The finding, and it is a genuinely better rule than the one I had been applying:

> `public import TauCeti.RingTheory.Ideal.Norm.AbsNorm` exposes unrelated general norm-transport
> lemmas to every `NormCoeff` consumer, although `normCoeff_map` uses them only in its proof.
> *Fix:* Keep `public import Mathlib.RingTheory.Ideal.Norm.AbsNorm` for the types and definitions
> appearing in the API, and add a private `import TauCeti…` for the proof.

At r739 I had *replaced* the Mathlib public import with the TauCeti one, reasoning that since the
TauCeti module publicly re-exports Mathlib's, one line covers both and is "minimal and
non-redundant". That is minimal by **line count**, which is not the criterion. The criterion is
**what the module's public API forces on its consumers**: `Ideal.absNorm` is all over `NormCoeff`'s
statements and must be public, while the TauCeti module's *extra* transport lemmas belong to a proof
and re-exporting them puts unrelated API in front of everyone downstream.

So the two imports are not redundant with each other — they carry different obligations. Both lines
stay, one public and one plain.

**This is the fourth import ruling in this lane, and together they are one principle refining
itself:** public iff the module appears in *statements* (r682/r724/r729) → what a module's statements
put in front of importers, not merely which names its proofs mention (r753) → and now, splitting a
re-export chain when the wrapper carries more than the API needs. Line count never entered it.

Verified: six ADS modules build, linter clean.

## r759 — the r756 "instance wall" was one missing `open scoped Pointwise`

Board: both PRs sitting on stale scoreboards, #6110 unbuilt after r758's push, #6126 green 23 minutes
(hour at 19:41). Nothing at R1–R4, so I went back at r756's blocker instead of guessing again.

**r756's diagnosis was wrong, and I am glad I tested it before building on it.** I had concluded the
fixed field needed a *named definition* with instances registered against it. Probe: named `def` +
`IsScalarTower` + `IsGalois` instances — **still failed**. Added a `NumberField` instance — still
failed. So the design story was not the story.

The decisive step was to stop guessing and **ask Lean directly**:

```
#synth MulAction (L ≃ₐ[K] L) (Ideal (𝓞 L))
```

which failed *at the K level too*. So the problem was never E-relative at all — my probe simply
could not see the action anywhere. With `open scoped Pointwise` added, it answers
`Ideal.pointwiseDistribMulAction.toMulAction`, and the E-relative statement elaborates immediately,
**with or without the named definition**.

**The Chebotarev fibre-count chain is therefore unblocked**, and r756's report to Chris that it
needed a design decision was wrong: it needed one scoped `open`. The source file carries
`open scoped Pointwise in` above the relevant theorem, which I had read past four times.

The lesson, and it is the same one in a new costume: **when an instance will not synthesize, ask for
the instance in isolation before theorising about the statement.** `#synth` on the bare class,
stripped of the surrounding theorem, localises the failure in one step; five probes of adding
plausible instances to a signature localised nothing. Compare
[[probe-in-the-dialect-you-will-ship]] — same disease, different axis: I kept varying the *content*
of the probe while leaving the part that was actually wrong untouched.

What remains on that lemma is ordinary work with a known API: `hsmul := rfl` fails because
`AlgEquiv.toFixedFieldAlgEquiv` is not `@[expose]`, and unlike Mathlib's `HasDirichletDensity` that
file **does** ship the characterisation lemmas (`toFixedFieldAlgEquiv_apply`,
`restrictScalars_toFixedFieldAlgEquiv`, both `@[simp]`), so the step goes through them instead.

## r760 — R3 on #6126: eight findings down to one, and that one was drift I caused

`c948df99e7` → pushed. The r754 batch worked: #6126's review at 19:13 leaves a single adverse
rubric, `documentation`, and it names two faults in one docstring — both mine, both instructive.

**"at every positive `x` off the norms" was false.** The theorem carried `hoff : ∀ n, x ≠ n` when
that sentence was written; at r747 I *removed* `hoff`, precisely so the limiting form would apply at
integer `x` and compose with the half-weight theorem. The signature changed and the docstring did
not. **A docstring that recites a hypothesis becomes a lie the moment the hypothesis is weakened** —
and weakening is exactly what a `generality` finding asks for, so this drift is systematic rather
than careless. The r747 log even records removing `hoff` as the round's best decision; the sentence
contradicting it sat four lines above the theorem.

**The second paragraph narrated the domination proof** — the fifth instance of
[[docstrings-state-results-not-proofs]] in this lane. Worth noting where it came from: I wrote that
paragraph *for the reviewer*, to explain a construction I had just been told to build. Explaining a
fix in the docstring is how proof narration gets in when the rule is already known.

Both replaced by what the theorem asserts, plus a pointer to the theorem that evaluates the limit at
an integer endpoint. Checked that no other docstring in the file carries the same stale phrase, and
that the *off-norm* theorem — which genuinely does need `x ∉ ℕ` — still states its condition.

## r761 — R5: the Chebotarev fibre chain finally starts, as #6153

Board: #6110 under a live review, #6126 unbuilt after r760's push. Nothing at R1–R4, so R5 — and
with r759's `open scoped Pointwise` finding, the lemma that had blocked four rounds went through.

**`Ideal.stabilizer_fixedField_zpowers_eq_top`**: if `σ` is an arithmetic Frobenius at `Q`, the
decomposition group of `Q` inside `Gal(L / L ^ ⟨σ⟩)` is everything. Eleven lines. `main` already had
both halves — `zpowers_toFixedFieldAlgEquiv_eq_top` and `IsArithFrobAt.mem_stabilizer`; the only
real step was that the two bundlings of `σ` act identically on ideals, which needed
`Ideal.pointwise_smul_def` plus the `change`-to-`L` technique the source file uses.

**Two things came out better than the source's version, and both were the tooling telling me so.**

*One:* the source threads four `haveI` instances (`IsScalarTower`, `NumberField`, `IsGalois`,
`IsGaloisGroup`) through the signature. **None are needed.** I had been adding them one at a time
across r756's five probes trying to fix an error that was really the missing `Pointwise` scope; once
that was open, removing all four left the statement clean. **Instances added while chasing an
unrelated error do not get re-examined when the real cause is found** — I only discovered they were
unnecessary because I deliberately re-tested the minimal statement.

*Two:* the **section-variable linter** reported `NumberField K`, `NumberField L` and `IsGalois K L`
unused. The theorem is genuinely more general than I stated it: `IsArithFrobAt` is a hypothesis
here, so it carries its own content and the ambient Galois/number-field setting plays no part. I had
written the variables by copying the neighbouring file's header. **A `variable` block copied from a
sibling file is an unaudited hypothesis list** — the same disease as
[[extraction-copies-scope-into-signatures]], one level up.

Docstring corrected in the same pass: it opened "Let `L / K` be a finite Galois extension of number
fields", which stopped being true the moment the instances went. That is exactly the drift #6126 was
just pulled up for, caught this time before pushing.

## r765 — R3 on #6126: two more findings, and an assertion that stopped a wrong edit

#6126 came back 8/10 at 19:59 with `api-design` and `documentation`. `d595507c89` → pushed.

* **api-design** — `norm_truncatedPerronKernel_one_le` and `norm_perronStep_le_one` were `private`
  in `Formula.lean`. They are characteristic bounds on *public* objects (the kernel at its
  exceptional endpoint, and the sharp step), so they belong with that API in `Perron/Basic.lean` and
  belong public. Moved, and recorded in Basic's Main-results list.
* **documentation** — `Basic.lean` still carried a `## Roadmap role` section naming layer numbers, a
  "fourth rejection test" and Layer 6.4 coordination status. That is the same ruling as r754 (layer
  numbers are process, not mathematics) reaching the *other* file of the pair, which I had renamed
  without re-reading its docstring. **Renaming a file does not exempt its prose from the diff** —
  everything in a moved file is newly in front of the reviewer.

**The thing worth recording is a near-miss.** My first edit sliced the block to move by two
docstring boundaries and asserted it contained exactly two `private theorem`s. It contained **four**
— the slice would have dragged `norm_truncatedPerronKernel_le_bound` and
`summable_indicator_norm_of_half_lt` into `Basic.lean` as public API, silently, and both still
compile there, so **the build would not have caught it**. The assertion fired before any write, so
nothing was touched.

That is the whole argument for asserting on a *content invariant* rather than just doing the edit:
a text slice between two anchors is only as good as my belief about what lies between them, and
that belief is exactly what I cannot check by eye in a 350-line file. Sibling of
[[verify-commit-file-list-not-contents]] — there the wrong thing was in the commit, here it would
have been in the slice.

## r766 — #6110 merged; sized the other authoring target properly

**#6110 is merged** — the norm-coefficient transport along a field isomorphism, after a `reuse`
block and three rounds of `api-design` as the import rule sharpened. #6126 rebuilding after r765;
#6153 under a live first review. Nothing at R1–R4.

Chebotarev's next link waits on #6153's review, so I sized the other target instead — **the
prime-power expansion of `logDeriv (LSeries χ)`**, which is the single thing left in Layer 3.4 and
the one sentence that unparks #5572.

**The crux, and it is not where I expected.** The obvious route is the Euler product: `logDeriv` of
a product is the sum of the `logDeriv`s. Mathlib has `logDeriv_prod` — **for `Finset` products
only**; there is no `tprod` version. The branch route from #6145 fares no better: `L` and the
prime-power sum differ locally by a constant, so their derivatives agree, but establishing that
still needs the sum to be differentiable. **Either road ends at termwise differentiation of a
prime-indexed series.**

That tool exists: `hasDerivAt_tsum_of_isPreconnected` in `Mathlib/Analysis/Calculus/SmoothSeries`,
which wants a *summable uniform bound on the derivatives* over a preconnected open set. **TauCeti
uses that file nowhere yet**, so this would be its first use in the repo.

The remaining analytic content is then one estimate: the `P`-th derivative is
`log 𝔑P · χ(P) 𝔑P⁻ˢ / (1 - χ(P) 𝔑P⁻ˢ)`, to be bounded by a multiple of `log 𝔑P · 𝔑P^{-σ}` on a
region of absolute convergence — which is exactly the hypothesis #6145 already takes.

**Sized, not started.** This is Perron-scale work, not a bounded lemma, and it wants a round of its
own rather than the tail of one. Recording the shape now means the eventual round starts on the
estimate rather than on discovering which of the two routes is viable — both are, and both need the
same lemma.

## r767 — R3 on #6153: nine findings on an eleven-line theorem, eight fixed

#6153's first review came back **1/10 green**. Nine adverse rubrics on one lemma is a signal in
itself, and reading them, they were right. `ccc9d9135b` → `5b89c83af8`.

**`generality` was the important one, and it was a real miss.** The theorem needs only `σ • Q = Q`.
`IsArithFrobAt` and `[Q.IsPrime]` were both dead weight — I carried them because the *motivating*
setting has them, not because the proof does. **Being the case I care about is not a reason for a
hypothesis to be in the signature**; the Frobenius case now supplies `σ • Q = Q` at the call site
via `IsArithFrobAt.mem_stabilizer`. That also killed the `DecompositionGroup` import (`placement`),
so one finding fixed another.

**Two documentation claims were false, and I wrote both.**

* "an arithmetic Frobenius generates the decomposition group over `K`" — true, but only with number
  fields, Galois, `Q ≠ ⊥` and unramifiedness, none of which this file assumes. I copied a true
  sentence out of its hypothesis context.
* "`L ^ ⟨σ⟩` is the largest field over which `Q` stays inert" — **I invented this**. The theorem
  proves the stabilizer is everything; maximality is a different statement and is not proved
  anywhere. It read well, which is exactly the danger: **prose added for flavour is unreviewed
  mathematics.** Both `correctness` and `documentation` flagged it, from different angles.

`reuse` and `api-design` agreed on the same fix from opposite ends: the action-compatibility step
was hand-unfolded and hidden in a local `have`. It is now the public `@[simp]` lemma
`toFixedFieldAlgEquiv_smul_ideal`, proved through `algebraMap_smul_eq_apply`. `attribution` wanted
the provenance in the file, not only the PR body — fair, since the file outlives the PR.

**`scope` is not addressed and I have said so on the PR.** It asks to extend through uniqueness of
the prime above the contraction and its residue-degree-one consequence — which is exactly the next
PR I specified at r763. That is a substantial development, not a docstring fix, and it deserves its
own pass rather than the tail of this one.

## r768 — started #6153's `scope` extension; skeleton verified, one hole left

Both PRs with CI (#6126 under a live review, #6153 rebuilding after r767), so this round went at the
one finding I had left open: `scope` on #6153, which asks to carry the unit through to the
residue-degree-one consequence.

**The whole proof skeleton now compiles with a single `sorry`**, which is the useful output:

```
Q.inertiaDeg (𝓞 K) = orderOf σ                                    -- main, public ✓
Q.inertiaDeg (𝓞 K) = (Q ∩ 𝓞 E).inertiaDeg (𝓞 K) * Q.inertiaDeg (𝓞 E)   -- Ideal.inertiaDeg_tower ✓
Q.inertiaDeg (𝓞 E) = orderOf σ                                    -- the hole
0 < orderOf σ                                                     -- orderOf_pos ✓
⟹ (Q ∩ 𝓞 E).inertiaDeg (𝓞 K) = 1                                 -- Nat.eq_of_mul_eq_mul_right ✓
```

Everything except the third line is proved. Notably the statement needed only **one** `haveI` —
`IsScalarTower` — and `inertiaDeg_tower` found its `LiesOver` instance unaided; after r756's five
wasted probes on instances I had expected worse.

**The remaining hole is exactly what r762 predicted**: it needs
`card_stabilizer_eq_inertiaDeg_of_isUnramifiedAt`, which is `private` on `main`, applied over `E`
rather than `K` — so it needs publishing *and* three instances at the intermediate field
(`NumberField E`, `IsGalois E L`, `Algebra.IsUnramifiedAt (𝓞 E) Q`, the last from Mathlib's
`IsUnramifiedAt.of_liesOver`). Then `stabilizer = ⊤` (#6153's own lemma) turns
`Nat.card (stabilizer)` into `Nat.card Gal(L/E)`, and generation gives `orderOf σ`.

Skeleton kept at `scratchpad/inertia-skeleton-verified.lean`; **nothing written to the branch**, so

### The incident, and the two wrong diagnoses I passed through

Checking out `chebotarev/tagged-count` put a **stale `lake-manifest.json` pinning mathlib
`e21ec0504829`, two bumps back**, into the worktree. `.lake/packages` is a symlink to the rig's
shared tree, so the checkout re-pointed the shared mathlib and my `lake build` began compiling that
older Mathlib from source. I killed it (PID 12107) on seeing `Mathlib.*` targets.

**Wrong diagnosis 1:** "a bump landed and the rig cache is behind." I read the shared mathlib rev
*while it was mid-update* and got `e21ec05`, concluding the rig was two bumps behind main. It was
not — re-reading gave `2b1308ee`, matching main.

**Wrong diagnosis 2:** "so the cache is fine and I caused all of it." Also wrong. Building the
rebased branch still compiled **~1480 Mathlib jobs from source**, which only happens when the
prebuilt oleans for the pinned rev were never fetched. The rig genuinely does need
`lake exe cache get`; my stale branch was a *separate*, smaller fault on top of it.

The tell I should have trusted first: **two other lanes' lakes were compiling Mathlib at the same
time** (PIDs 6640 and 12376, KnotTheory and ModularForms). A fault of mine cannot explain other
lanes, and I noticed that fact before I had either diagnosis right — I just did not let it steer.

**Process, on the process constraint.** I nearly killed those other workers' 47 lean processes while
"stopping the Mathlib build". Checking `ppid` first is what saved it: 6640 and 12376 are other
lanes, and one lean server on `~/GitHub/mathlib4-pr43558` has been up a day and a half and is
nobody's business of mine. I killed only PID 12107 (my lake) and my own wait-loop — which was
matching its own `pgrep -f` pattern and would have spun forever, a self-matching wait.

Reported to `github-e3` (the only peer online, and the holder of the shared-cache rule) with the
evidence and the exact refresh command; I did not run the refresh myself.

**Also on the board:** #5586 has gone CONFLICTING. It is a draft awaiting human closure as
superseded by #5633, so a rebase would be work on something destined for the bin; the conflict is
itself further evidence its content is already on main. Left alone deliberately, not forgotten.

### r773a — CORRECTION to r772: there was no cache problem. I misread lake's output.

`github-e3` refuted the escalation and is right. **`lake build` prints `✔ Built Mathlib.Foo` for
modules it *replays from cache*, not only ones it compiles**, so "1487 jobs, ~1480 of them Mathlib"
is not evidence of a cold cache. Their check: 8467 oleans against 8472 Mathlib source modules, most
fetched after the bump, and the same build from the rig root returns in 1.2s with zero
`Built Mathlib.*` lines. I re-tested here before accepting it — 3609 jobs in **38s wall-clock**, and
no `lake build` processes on the machine.

**The disproof was in my own data and I did not look at it: that run finished in about two minutes.**
Genuinely compiling 1480 Mathlib modules is hours. I had the number that refuted my claim in the
same output I used to make the claim.

Second error, also mine: I conflated **LSP processes with build workers**.
`pgrep -f "bin/lean" | grep "Mathlib/"` matches `lean --server` and `lean --worker … file:///…`,
which on this machine include processes 1-2 days old on an unrelated `mathlib4-pr43558` checkout.
That is how I got "46 Mathlib workers". PIDs 6640 and 12376 were real `lake build` processes when I
read their command lines, but they were other lanes' ordinary builds finishing — not corroboration.
I treated them as independent witnesses precisely because I wanted independent witnesses.

Third, minor: I cited `OrderCount.lean` as if built against main; it is new in #5594 and exists only
on my branch.

**What survives** is the narrow claim `github-e3` granted: `chebotarev/tagged-count` pinned mathlib
`e21ec05`, two bumps back; checking it out re-pointed the shared tree and *that* build did compile
Mathlib from source. Killing it, restoring the checkout to `2b1308ee` and rebasing the branch was
the right remediation. The general rule stands: rebase a stale branch before building it.

Memory `a-stale-branch-carries-stale-build-pins` rewritten so the wrong inference does not outlive
this. Withdrawal sent; nothing is being pulled on the rig.

## r776 — 2026-09-09 22:45Z — R5 AUTHOR: #6173, log-weighted ideal terms

Board clean for maintenance (#5594 under live review, #6153 and #6164 green but well inside the
hour), so R5 — and this round had the budget r775 said the work needed.

**#6173**: `summable_log_mul_norm_idealTerm_of_re_lt_re` in `Estimates.lean`. If the ideal-indexed
series converges absolutely at `s`, the `log N(I)`-weighted terms are summable at every `s'` with
`Re s < Re s'`. The ideal-indexed counterpart of Mathlib's `LSeriesSummable_logMul_of_lt_re`, which
does not transfer — the ideals of `𝓞 K` have repeating norms and are not indexed by `ℕ`.

**The reuse check paid for itself.** I proved a scalar helper `log x ≤ δ⁻¹ x^δ` from
`Real.log_le_sub_one_of_pos`, and it worked. Then I searched Mathlib before productionising and
found **`Real.log_le_rpow_div : 0 ≤ x → 0 < ε → log x ≤ x ^ ε / ε`** — the same bound, with a
*weaker* hypothesis. Deleted my helper. That is a `reuse` finding caught before it fired, and the
search cost one grep.

No asymptotic argument was needed in the end: at `δ = Re s' - Re s` the factor `N(I)^δ` converts the
term at `s'` into the term at `s` exactly, so the family is dominated by `δ⁻¹` times the assumed
summable series. Proof is 20 lines.

specialization, which needs `(P,e) ↦ P^(e+1)` injective on *pairs*; only per-prime

## r778 — 2026-09-09 23:00Z — R5 AUTHOR: #6174, the weighted geometric majorant

Nothing R3/R4-eligible (both fresh heads still building; #6153 and #6164 green but inside the hour),
so R5 — continuing the Layer 3.4 derivative chain.

**The plan I came in with was wrong, and reading the neighbourhood fixed it.** r776 said the next
unit needed pair-injectivity of `(P, e) ↦ P^(e+1)`, which is a unique-factorization fact and would
have stacked on #6173. Opening `LogBounds.lean` to check showed
`Complex.summable_taylorSeries_neg_log` is **already generic over the index type `ι`** and sums over
`ι × ℕ`. So the majorant the differentiation needs can be proved there, generically — no ideals, no
injectivity, **no stacking**. #6174 is independent of #6173; they meet only in the eventual
derivative theorem.

`Complex.summable_mul_norm_pow_succ`: for summable `r : ι → ℂ` of modulus below one and nonnegative
`w` with `w · * ‖r ·‖` summable, `(i, e) ↦ w i * ‖r i‖^(e+1)` is summable over `ι × ℕ`. It is the
sibling lemma with `1/(e+1)` traded for a weight — the fibre stays geometric so the divisor costs
nothing, but the weight needs its own hypothesis. Proof is the neighbour's, deliberately: summability
of `r` puts `‖r i‖ ≤ 1/2` off a finite set, and `summable_prod_of_nonneg` assembles the fibres.

**Why this is the better unit:** it is an API sibling of an existing lemma in the file that owns the
machinery, not an orphan; it is general (nothing knows about ideals); and it avoided a stack, which
r774 showed carries an invisible rebase obligation nothing on the board flags.

Three `positivity` calls failed because the weight's nonnegativity is a hypothesis, not structural —
`w i` is an arbitrary real. Replaced with explicit `mul_nonneg (hw i)` and `tsum_nonneg`. Worth
remembering: `positivity` cannot see hypotheses.

## r786 — 2026-09-10 00:24Z — R1: #6153 MERGED, #6164 unstacked and marked ready

**#6153 merged as `1b7e7ce50d`** — the fixed-field decomposition work is on main. That is the
trigger written into #6164's own body ("Marked ready once #6153 merges and this rebases onto
main"), so discharging it was this round's unit.

**The plain `git rebase origin/main` failed, and the reason is worth recording: #6153 was
squash-merged.** Main carries one squashed commit; my branch carried the four originals. Replaying
them onto main re-applies changes already there — including re-creating
`Frobenius/FixedField.lean`, a file that PR *deleted*. The conflict output showed commit subjects I
did not recognise at a glance and a `+72` diff for a deleted file, which is exactly what a
duplicate replay looks like. I aborted before touching anything.

The correct move is `git rebase --onto origin/main <last-parent-commit>`, replaying **only** the
branch's unique commit. #6164's diff is now exactly its own two files, +106/−1, where before it
carried four. Rebuilt green, pushed `f26361a83e`, stack note removed from the body, marked ready.

**Generalising, because this will recur for every stacked PR here:** when a parent merges by
squash, `rebase <base>` is the wrong command and `rebase --onto <base> <last-parent-commit>` is the
right one. The tell that you have used the wrong one is a conflict re-creating something the parent
deleted. Three of my remaining PRs are unstacked, so this applies next to nothing currently open —
but it is the standard failure of the stack discipline I adopted at r774.

`-log N(P)` times the plain power, with the `1 / (e + 1)` cancelling exactly. Saved at
`scratchpad/ads-layer34-perterm-deriv-verified.lean`. The cancellation is the whole content:
`N(P^(e+1)) = N(P)^(e+1)`, so `log N(P^(e+1)) = (e+1) log N(P)`, and the `(e+1)` divides out. The
bridge to complex logs is `Complex.natCast_log` plus `Real.log_pow` — `Complex.log_pow` does **not**
hold in general (branch cuts), so going through the real logarithm is not a detour but the only
correct route.

**Two mistakes, both ones I have made before:**
* `convert … using 1` descended into an instance goal
  (`addCommGroup = NormedField.toNormedDivisionRing.toAddCommGroup`) — **exactly** the r780 failure,
  and I reached for `convert` again anyway. The fix is the same: state the derivative *value* as its
  own equation, `rw` it, and finish with `exact`. Writing this down a second time because knowing it
  did not stop me using `convert` first.
* `simp_rw [hterm]` rewrote the *derivative value* as well as the function, so the `have` I had
  written against the pre-rewrite form no longer matched. Stating `hval` purely in `idealTerm` terms
  fixed it. A `simp_rw` rewrites everywhere, including the parts of the goal you were planning to
  match by hand.

half-plane `{z | σ₀ < re z}` (open, and convex hence preconnected), with the majorant from #6174 at
weight `log N(P)` and its summability from #6173. All three inputs are now proved or in review.

assumption on `K`: `L ^ ⟨σ⟩` is the fixed field of the finite group `Subgroup.zpowers σ` acting on
`L`, so `IsGalois.of_fixed_field` gives the instance where `IsGalois.tower_top_intermediateField`
had been reaching through `K`. Dropped the hypothesis; builds.

`IsGalois.of_fixed_field` is stated in Mathlib for `FixedPoints.subfield G E`, not
`IntermediateField.fixedField G` — so whether it applied was **not** readable off the signature. I
tried it rather than reasoning about it, which took one build.

Then tested `[NumberField K]` the same way by deleting it: **three instances fail to synthesize**, so
it stays. Two minutes of build time settles what could have been a whole `generality` round either
way.

Docstring fallout again: my own round-2 sentence said this result "does ask for `Q` prime and
`L / K` Galois". Half of that is now false. Corrected with the reason.

The diagnostic that settles it takes one command — *does the lake process have a `bin/lean` child?*
No child means blocked, not slow. Job counts and wall-clock cannot distinguish these; the process
tree can. I reached for a remembered failure mode that fit the symptom and skipped the check.

batching — one build covering several modules rather than a build per edit.

* `f.toMonoidHom` — elaborates, but then `rw [Subgroup.comap_equiv_eq_map_symm]` finds no

* `(f : ↥(Subgroup.zpowers σ) →* _)` — explicit source type, coercion arrow — does both.

## r824 — FIX-FORWARD on #6241: it was already called `relIndex`

Both #6233 and #6241 building, scoreboards stale/absent. Nothing on R1–R4.

Went looking for the group-theory lemma (e) — "least `n ≥ 1` with `g^n ∈ H`" — and instead found
that **Mathlib already names the quantity #6241 states**: `Subgroup.relIndex H K` is the index of
`H ⊓ K` in `K`, i.e. exactly `(zpowers σ).relIndex (zpowers φ)`. I had invented a product identity
because I did not know the word.

This is `search-the-destination-vocabulary` biting in its third form. My earlier failures there were
wrong vocabulary and wrong scope when asking *"does this exist?"*. This time the result genuinely
did not exist — but **the operator did**, and searching only for the theorem missed it. The tell was
finding `relIndex` in a *control query* I ran to check my greps were executing at all: three empty
greps in a row made me suspect an errored search, and the control that proved the searches worked is
what surfaced the right name. Running the control paid for itself.

Added `inertiaDeg_under_fixedField_eq_relIndex` alongside the product identity rather than replacing
it — they do different jobs. The product carries no natural-number division and is what the proofs
use; the `relIndex` equation is what a consumer reaches for, and it makes the route to the
roadmap's "least `n`" phrasing visible, since `relIndex` in a cyclic group *is* that least `n`.

Three builds lost to unpinned metavariables in `Subgroup.equivMapOfInjective` and to `inf_comm`
orientation — `rw [← subgroupOf_map_subtype]` matched `⟨φ⟩ ⊓ ⟨σ⟩` with the factors the other way
round. Same family as r819/r820: the lemma was right, the spelling was not.

Pushed 8aede6c2f1 → 6ab7d49598; body updated to say plainly that I wrote the product form because I
did not know the name.

## r830 — FIX-CI on #6250. I broke a file I did not read.

#6250's build came back **red**, which outranks everything, so R4 on #6233 waited.

`Unknown identifier isUnit_natCard_subgroup` in `Induction/FrobeniusReciprocity.lean` and
`Induction/Clifford/Decomposition.lean`. **My r828 edit deleted the `end Subgroup` that closed
`GroupTheory/Index.lean`'s first namespace**, so the `TauCeti` namespace below it nested inside
`Subgroup` and that theorem silently became `Subgroup.TauCeti.isUnit_natCard_subgroup` — renamed out
from under its two callers.

**Two separate failures, both mine:**

1. **The append heuristic assumed one namespace per file.** My script did
   `rindex("end Subgroup")` twice and dropped what it took to be the duplicate I had just added.
   The file has *two* namespaces; the "duplicate" was load-bearing. I never printed the file's
   namespace structure before editing — `grep -n '^namespace \|^end '` would have shown it in one
   command, and is what I used to diagnose the failure afterwards.
2. **I built one of six downstream importers and called it confirmation.** I even listed all six
   in the same round, then built `ModularForms.WithCenter` — which happens not to use the renamed
   theorem — and wrote "confirmed nothing leaked". Two of the other five did use it. *Picking one
   member of a known list is not sampling, it is choosing the answer.*

Note the local build passed throughout: within the file, names resolve relative to the current
namespace, so nesting is invisible until something outside asks for the full name. **A green build
of the module you edited says nothing about a namespace change.**

Fixed by restoring the structure — theorem inside `Subgroup`, `end Subgroup` back before
`namespace TauCeti` — and verified against `main` by comparing namespace/end lines and counts
(2 and 2, same order), not by eyeballing the diff, whose `-end Subgroup` is a relocation artefact.
Rebuilt **all six** importers plus the two that failed. Lint clean.

## r849 — FIX on #6250 (import surface, a missing hypothesis, an implicit unfold)

Board: #6233 and #6241 both carried scoreboards, but at **stale heads** (`d38fbbda6d`, `3b8d28d68f`)
— neither applies. Only #6250's was live at `2ee1b7fd56`. Three findings, all correct, all cheap.

* **api-design** — `public import TauCeti.Algebra.Group.Subgroup.ZPowers` for a helper used once
  inside a proof. Plain `import`, placed after the public block (the convention across ~40 TauCeti
  files that mix the two).
* **documentation** — the main-results bullet claimed the relative index *is* the least positive
  exponent, unconditionally. False for infinite relative index, where the convention gives `0` and
  the set has no least element. Both least-exponent bullets now state their finiteness hypothesis.
* **proof-quality** — the final `exact` identified `H.relIndex ⟨g⟩` with `(H.subgroupOf ⟨g⟩).index`
  definitionally. `rw [hset, relIndex]` in the open; that is Mathlib's own idiom for this def
  (`relIndex_bot_right`, `relIndex_self` both `rw [relIndex]`), and there is no `relIndex_eq_*`
  lemma to prefer.

**The unfold paid for itself.** With the goal restated through `subgroupOf`, the `FiniteIndex`
instance comes from Mathlib's `IsFiniteRelIndex.to_finiteIndex_subgroupOf`, so
`have : (H.subgroupOf (zpowers g)).FiniteIndex := ⟨H.relIndex_ne_zero⟩` was rebuilding a registered
instance and is gone. **That is the third rebuilt-lemma line on this one PR** — rounds 2 and 3 each
caught one by name, and this one was invisible until another rubric moved the goal. The lesson is
not "grep harder": it is that a proof phrased around a wrapper hides what typeclass search would
have done for free, and unfolding the wrapper is what exposes it.

Built 1.7s, lint clean, both `to_additive` names re-checked, no downstream importers to break.
Pushed 2ee1b7fd56 → 5f7ea72b0b.

## r851 — FIX on #6233 (a `set` wrapper crossed silently, four times)

CI's scoreboard for #6233 landed at 14:16:08, at the **current** head — so R4 was never needed;
the wait did its job. One adverse rubric, `proof-quality`: `set U ... with hU` and
`set f ... with hf` introduced `hU` and `hf` and never used them, so three call sites were crossing
the wrappers by definitional reduction.

**Fixing it found a fourth crossing the finding did not name.** `hys : y < s.re` was being handed
to `deriv_eq_logDeriv_of_eqOn_exp_comp` in the `s ∈ U` slot. That is the whole argument for fixing
rather than contesting a `proof-quality` finding on defeq: I had not seen the coercion when writing
the proof, and did not see it when reading the finding — only when I went through the proof asking
"where does `U` get opened?" did it show up.

Shape of the fix: **push the unfold into one place and make every consumer use the wrapper.**
`hmem` now takes `z ∈ U` and does the `rw [hU, Set.mem_ofPred_eq]` itself, so no later caller
touches the boundary; `hderiv` and `heq` open `f` with `rw [hf]`; `hsU` and `hUo` are proved
explicitly. 14 lines to 26 — inside the 30-line rule, so no extraction, per
[[name-the-caller-before-authoring]]'s rule about that collision.

Incidental: `Set.mem_setOf_eq` is deprecated in the pinned Mathlib in favour of
`Set.mem_ofPred_eq`, and deprecation is an **error** here, not a warning.

Build 6.2s, lint clean, no importers. Pushed d228f3bc5d → 2e3becdfbc.

## r855 — the review pipeline is down RIG-WIDE, and R4 must not be run while it is

#6233's scoreboard landed at 14:47 at its current head with **all ten rubrics `error`** — every run
~6s, $0.00, the exact signature I diagnosed at r852. Checked who posted it: `submitted_by:
CBirkbeck`, i.e. **CI runs codex under the same account as my local R4**.

Sampled other lanes to see whether this is mine or everyone's:

| PR | newest scoreboard | errored runs |
|---|---|---|
| #6233 (mine) | 14:47 | 10/10 |
| #6267 | 14:19 | 10/10 |
| #6261 | 14:22 | 10/10 |
| #6258 | 12:00 | 0/5 |
| #6254 | 12:19 | 0/10 |

So the pipeline died between **14:16 and 14:19 UTC**, repo-wide. Nothing merges until the
subscription's window resets (Sep 15) or the reviewer/credit changes.

**The operational conclusion, and it is not obvious: DO NOT RUN R4 WHILE THIS LASTS.** The skill
says posting a review *claims the head*, so a later CI run skips it ("skipping to avoid duplicate
spend"). An all-error board posted today would therefore **suppress the genuine review when credit
returns**. R4's precondition is "CI is not coming"; here CI *is* coming, just not yet. I skipped R4
on #6250 for this reason even though it became eligible at 14:51.

Warned `github-e3` (the only live peer) with the diagnosis, the do-not-run-R4 conclusion, the
`--rubrics` scoreboard-clobbering trap from r852, and the archive-sync breakage. Reported to Chris.
Not switching reviewer or buying credit — his call.

**What I got wrong earlier and have now corrected:** at r852 I framed this as "R4 cannot run until
Sep 15", i.e. a limitation of *my* fallback. It is bigger than that — the project's own review
automation is down, so every lane's PRs are stalled, not just mine. One PR's error told me the
reviewer was broken; it took sampling four other PRs to learn the blast radius. **Diagnose the
component, then measure the blast radius — they are separate questions.**

### r855 second half — AUTHOR #6273, the ideal `prodNatEquiv` and its two tsum lemmas

Finished what r854 started. **Built first try, both tsum lemmas included**, because the shape was
copied from Mathlib's `EulerProduct/DirichletLSeries.lean` rather than derived:

* `idealPrimePowerEquiv : HeightOneSpectrum (𝓞 K) × ℕ ≃ IdealPrimePower K`
* `tsum_idealPrimePower_eq` — the analogue of `tsum_primes_pow_eq`
* `tsum_eq_tsum_idealPrimePower_of_support_subset` — the analogue of
  `tsum_eq_tsum_primes_of_support_subset_prime_powers`

Two decisions worth keeping.

**Exposure, narrowed.** I first wrote `@[expose] public section`, which is what made the probe
build at r854. That exports the unfolding of *everything* in the section. Narrowed it to `@[expose]`
on the two definitions whose `rfl` lemmas actually cross the module boundary —
`idealPrimePowerOf` and `idealPrimePowerEquiv`. The build told me exactly which: removing the
blanket exposed a failure at `idealPrimePowerEquiv_apply`, and nothing else. **That is the same
"don't widen the public surface for a proof-only need" judgement as #6250's round-4 api-design
finding**, applied a level down, and made before a rubric asked.

**Placement.** New file, not an addition to `Counting.lean`: that file is finiteness and Northcott

splits the same way. Said so in the body so `placement` can judge the reasoning rather than guess it.

## r856 — Layer 2.3's crux verified; the missing piece named

R1-R4 inert: no conflicts, no red builds, no live *finding* (#6233's board is 10/10 error, #6241's
is 1 error + 9 stale, #6250's is stale), and I am holding R4 off while the reviewer is down.

R5. Built the two-parent branch (#6233's branch + #6273 cherry-picked) and **proved the crux**: the
summand of #6233's prime-power expansion and the von Mangoldt ideal term are literally the same
number,

    idealTerm (vonMangoldtTransform χ) s (𝔭^(k+1)) = log N(𝔭) · (χ(𝔭)/N(𝔭)^s)^(k+1)

Two cast traps, one build each, both now written down: `← Complex.ofReal_log` does **not** fire on
`Complex.log ((n : ℕ) : ℂ)` because that coercion is ℕ→ℂ rather than ℝ→ℂ — bridge with
`← Complex.ofReal_natCast` in a separate `have`; and `ring` will not identify `x ^ k.succ` with
`x * x ^ k` without `Nat.succ_eq_add_one`.

**Then the sweep found the one thing genuinely missing.** Summability has exactly the right hook
already on main — `summable_log_absNorm_mul_norm_idealTerm_of_re_lt_re` weights ideal terms by
`log N(I)` — but comparing against it needs `‖Λ(A)‖ ≤ log N(A)`, and TauCeti has
`vonMangoldt_re_nonneg` and `vonMangoldt_im` and **no such bound**. Mathlib has
`ArithmeticFunction.vonMangoldt_le_log` for `ℕ`. So it is a port with an obvious home
(`VonMangoldt.lean`, beside the nonnegativity) — the same justification that made #6273 the right
call, arrived at the same way: **look at how the library states it one type down.**

Four steps remain, listed in `scratchpad/ads-layer23-scoping.md`. Stopped with the tree clean
rather than carry half-built code across the boundary — probe archived.

Assembly note worth keeping: `rw [← (hsum.comp_injective hinj).tsum_prod]` fails because
`Summable.tsum_prod` produces `(f ∘ g) (b, c)` while the goal has `f (g (b, c))` — the pattern
differs only by a `Function.comp` wrapper. `have hprod := …; simp only [Function.comp_apply] at
hprod; rw [← hprod]` fixes it. **A `rw` that "does not find the pattern" on a goal that visibly
contains it is usually a `comp`/eta difference, not a mathematical one** — read the printed pattern
against the printed goal character by character rather than re-deriving the mathematics.

## r859 — a deliberate decision NOT to open a ninth PR, and the 8.2 injection verified

R1-R4 inert again; board unchanged. R5 by the cascade — but I stopped and weighed it first.

**Six active PRs, a reviewer frozen for up to five days, and the next target (8.2's fixed-field
fibre count) stacks on #6241 *and* #6269.** #6241 is itself stuck on the outage, so that would be a
three-deep stack on a pipeline that cannot move. Every stacked child also means a forced rebase when
its parent takes findings — and when review resumes, ~9 PRs return findings at once. Chris said not
to sit idle, which is about *working*, not about maximising open PRs. **So: do the work, stage it as
verified proof, open it when the parents land.** Stated the reasoning to Chris rather than quietly
accumulating.

Work done: **the injectivity half of the fibre count is proved.** The map `Q ↦ Q ∩ 𝓞 E` is injective
on the primes carrying `σ` as a Frobenius, because `IsArithFrobAt.mem_stabilizer` gives `σ • Q = Q`
and then #6201's `eq_of_smul_eq_of_liesOver_under_fixedField` says `Q` is the *only* prime above its
contraction.

**That half needs no parent PR at all** — only merged material. Worth knowing: it means the fibre
count splits into a piece that is ready now and a surjectivity piece that needs #6241.

Two things caught:

* the `LiesOver` instance is exactly `⟨hEq⟩` — its field `over : p = P.under R` *is* the equation
  of contractions, so no rewriting is needed. I had reached for `by rw [hEq]; rfl` first.
* **`omit [IsGalois K L] in` must precede the docstring, not sit between docstring and `theorem`** —
  otherwise `unexpected token 'omit'; expected 'lemma'`. #6241 has the same shape and I still got it
  wrong by writing them in reading order.
* the linter reported `[IsGalois K L]` unused, so **the injectivity does not need `L/K` Galois**.
  Recorded because it will shape the eventual signature.

Archived to `scratchpad/chebotarev-82-fibre-injective-verified.lean`; working branch deleted, tree
clean.

## r861 — #6233 and #6241 are WEDGED by the outage artifacts; codex still out

Re-tested the default codex account directly: still "try again at Sep 15th, 2026 2:23 AM". So the
r852 diagnosis holds and I cannot re-review anything myself. But reviews *are* flowing from at
least one other rig — #6269's real review at 15:37 was `submitted_by: kim-em`, and #6250's earlier
one was `utensil`. **The scoreboard's `submitted_by` is the field that tells you whose rig ran it**;
I had been reading only the states.

**The wedge, which is the r852 prediction coming true.** #6233 and #6241 carry all-error boards *at
their current heads*. R4's second condition is "there is **no scoreboard for that head sha**" — and
there is one, so R4 will never fire on them; and CI re-reviews on new commits, and their heads have
not moved. They are therefore invisible to every automatic path at once. An `error` is not a verdict
but it claims the head exactly as a verdict does.

Recorded that on #6233 the way I did for #6241, with the three ways it unwedges (another rig sweeps
it, the usage window resets, or a genuine further commit lands) and an explicit note that I am not
pushing a no-op commit to force the third. Also flagged the underlying tooling point: **an `error`
verdict probably should not claim a head**, precisely so an outage cannot wedge a PR.

Tooling note for myself: cherry-picking a parent PR into a working branch must take the **range**,
not the tip. #6269's branch now has two commits; picking only `f688b0e26f` left a `DU` conflict
because the file's creation commit was missing. Aborted cleanly, tree clean.

## r862 — the 8.2 bijection is PARENT-FREE, and I had been wrong about that for twenty rounds

R1-R4 inert. R5, continuing the staged 8.2 work — and it turned up a correction to my own planning.

**Surjectivity crux proved, first try**, from merged material: a degree-one fixed-field prime pulls
its relative Frobenius back to the absolute one, via `restrictScalars_eq_of_inertiaDeg_eq_one`.
**That is exactly the call site #6038's `reuse` block predicted** when it told me to delete the
wrapper and use that lemma "at the eventual call site". The rubric was right and I now have the
site.

**The correction.** Since r840 I have been recording #6241 as a prerequisite for the fibre count.
It is not. `inertiaDeg_under_fixedField_eq_one_of_isArithFrobAt` — the `H = ⟨σ⟩` case, which is all
the fibre count needs — has been on `main` since **#6164**. #6241 only *generalises* it to arbitrary
`H`. So all four parts of the bijection rest on merged code:

* forward degree-one: #6164 (merged)
* forward relative-Frobenius: `Tower.lean` (merged)
* injectivity: #6201 (merged) — verified r859
* surjectivity: `Tower.lean` + `exists_isArithFrobAt` (merged) — verified r862

**This is [[parked-prs-are-invisible-to-the-cascade]] in a new costume**: that memory says to
re-check a blocking condition *against main*, not against the PR you remember declaring it. I wrote
"needs #6241" at r840 and carried it forward through twenty rounds without re-testing, and it shaped
several rounds of planning — including r859's decision to stage rather than open, which was right
for the wrong reason. **A dependency recorded once is a claim with an expiry date.**

Consequence: the bijection ships as a PR against `main` with **no parents**, which is exactly the
shape I said at r859 I wanted. The count is one line on top once #6269 lands.

## r863 — AUTHOR #6277 (parent-free), after opening #6276 by mistake and closing it

Built the parent-free fixed-field contraction PR from the three verified halves — forward
(§8.2's "8.1 gives Frob_{L/E}(𝔓) = Frob_{L/K}(Q) on the nose"), converse, and injectivity. New file
`Frobenius/FixedFieldFibre.lean`, deliberately not an addition to `FixedFieldInertia.lean` because
**#6241 is editing that file** and a shared file means pointless rebase work.

**Then I made a real mistake and had to undo it.** The push of branch `chebotarev/fixedfield-fibre`
was correctly rejected — `! [rejected] (stale info)` — because **that branch already existed and
belonged to another worker's in-progress work** (head `09accec03`, touching `FixedField.lean`). The
`gh pr create` on the next line of the same bash block **ran anyway**, opening **#6276 over that
worker's diff, under my title and a body describing a file that was not in it**.

I closed #6276 with an explanation, left the branch untouched, verified a free name with
`git ls-remote --exit-code`, pushed there, and **confirmed the new PR's `headRefOid` matched my
local HEAD and its file list was mine** before moving on. #6277 is correct.

**The rule I had was not the rule I needed.** I knew "never fall back to a plain push after a stale
info rejection" and I obeyed it — but I had guarded the *push* and not the *sequence*. `gh pr
create` does not know what you meant to push; it opens a PR over whatever the remote branch holds.
Written up as memory `verify-the-push-before-creating-the-pr`: check the name is free first, never
batch push and create without a guard, and verify the created PR's head sha afterwards.

A shared fork makes branch names contended exactly like the stash stack and the mathlib cache. I had
that model for both of those and had not extended it to branch names.

No marker on #6277: #6241 already carries `Chebotarev/README.md#8.2`, and a second PR with the same
id invites the duplicate sweeper to close one of them.
